title: Nurturing Chaozhou Mackerel Bao
description: A briny, molten bao that showcases the rich flavor of fresh mackerel, wrapped in a fluffy long‑fermentation dough, perfect for a high‑protein meal.

ingredients.name: Marinade
ingredients.amount: soy sauce 15g, oyster sauce 5g, sesame oil 3g, chili garlic sauce 10g

instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together 250g warm water, 3g active dry yeast, and 5g salt until dissolved.
Add 300g bread flour and 1 tbsp vegetable oil, mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 8 minutes until smooth, then shape into a ball.
Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise at room temperature for 4 hours; then refrigerate overnight for long fermentation.
Trim 200g fresh mackerel fillet into 2cm cubes and pat dry.
Combine 30g water chestnuts, 20g scallions, and 10g ginger into a bowl; add the mackerel cubes, then pour the marinades and toss to coat.
Cover the marinated mix and let sit in the fridge for 30 minutes to absorb flavors.
Punch down the dough, divide into 8 equal portions, and roll each into a small circle about 7 cm in diameter.
Place a spoonful of the mackerel filling onto each dough circle, then fold the edges over to seal into buns.
Arrange the buns on a bamboo steamer lined with parchment, place the steamer over a pot of boiling water, cover, and steam for 15 minutes.
Remove the buns, sprinkle with 20g fresh coriander leaves and 10g white sesame seeds, and serve hot.
